clue.text: Quietly stick it back on outside: that's common sense

indicators.note: outside says the run of pieces before it is wrapped around the quiet letter

parts.note: to stick is to gum, as with glue

indicators.note: back tells us the little word it is to be read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
P is piano, the musical direction to play quietly

explanation.surface: Someone advises gluing a part back on, calling it simple common sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quietly' looks like an adverb for the sticking, but it is the musical P; 'back' and 'outside' are the two signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Gumption is native shrewdness or practical good judgement.

clue.text: Decorative artwork's instant appeal I caught

parts.note: a mo is a moment, an instant
SA is sex appeal
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A piece of art is said to have instant appeal that caught the narrator's eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A mosaic is a picture or pattern made of small coloured tiles, a decorative art form.

clue.text: A condition set out in second policy statement

indicators.note: in places the condition and the rearranged set inside the second

parts.note: a mo is a very short time, a second
an if is a condition, as in 'no ifs or buts'

indicators.note: set out means the letters of set are laid out afresh

explanation.surface: A condition is laid out in a party's policy document.
explanation.walkthrough: The article A grows an N before the vowel of 'if', so 'A condition' supplies AN IF; 'out' scrambles the next word and 'in' does the enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: A manifesto is a public declaration of a party's policies and aims.

clue.text: Murphy for one, we hear, is so unkempt!

indicators.note: we hear says the word is to be spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: murphy is slang for a potato, and tattie is the Scots word for a potato

explanation.surface: Someone named Murphy is mocked as scruffy.
explanation.walkthrough: Murphy looks like a surname; it is old slang for a potato (Irish associations), and TATTIE is the Scottish word for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Tatty means shabby and worn, a close synonym of unkempt.

clue.text: One changing colour that's extremely dreary, I hesitate to say

indicators.note: extremely asks for the extreme letters, the first and last of dreary

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation in speech

explanation.surface: Someone hesitantly calls something rather dreary.
explanation.definitionFit: A dyer is a person who dyes cloth, altering its colour.

clue.text: Profanation accountant's recalled, say, in anger

indicators.note: recalled, called back, turns the accountant's letters around

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant, so accountant's is CA'S

indicators.note: in puts the example abbreviation inside the word for anger

parts.note: to rile is to anger
eg (for example) is the usual crossword stand-in for say

explanation.surface: A profane outburst is blamed on an accountant recalled in fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' is the usual crossword cue for EG; 'recalled' turns only the accountant's letters, and 'in' does the enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacrilege is the violation of something sacred, which is what profanation means.

clue.text: Instrument old vicar transported round church

indicators.note: round says the shuffled letters go around the church abbreviation
transported means carried off, so the letters are moved into new places

explanation.surface: An elderly clergyman carries a keyboard instrument around the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transported' is the anagram signal (CLAVIORD), not travel; 'round' wraps those letters about the church abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A clavichord is an early keyboard instrument with strings struck by small brass blades.

clue.text: Possibly a club eccentric

definitions.meaning: one of the clubs suit in a deck is a playing ...
a comically odd person, a character

explanation.surface: Someone in a golf club or society is thought rather odd.
explanation.definitionFit: A card can be a club in a pack, and also an amusing oddball.

clue.text: Mountain where poet from East loses daughter?

indicators.note: loses says a letter is dropped from the word
read from the East means from right to left in an across clue, so the poet runs backwards

parts.note: Dante is the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: A question about the peak where a poet from the East parted with his daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from East' reverses DANTE to ETNAD, and 'loses' removes D.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is the active volcano on Sicily, a mountain.

clue.text: Disruptive cat is a lion on the rampage!

indicators.note: something on the rampage runs wild, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A big cat, a lion, running amok is causing trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rampage' rearranges CAT IS A LION.
explanation.definitionFit: Antisocial behaviour is disruptive and harmful to others.

clue.text: Revolutionary woman carrying about grand Chinese dress

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so the two names enclose the other pieces

parts.note: Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary
Sam is a woman's name, short for Samantha
on can mean about, concerning
G is the usual abbreviation for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A female revolutionary carries a grand Chinese gown around.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheongsam is a close-fitting Chinese dress with a high collar.

clue.text: Irritable BBC boss cutting viewer short

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so the boss goes inside
short says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: an eye is the organ that views
the head of the BBC is the Director-General, DG

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered head of the BBC cuts a viewer off mid-sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: The BBC's head is the Director-General, abbreviated DG; 'short' docks a letter and 'cutting' does the inserting.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgy means nervous and on edge, quick to irritation.

clue.text: Setback for wicked old woman

indicators.note: set back means put in reverse, so the wicked and old pieces are turned around together

parts.note: wicked means evil

explanation.surface: A wicked old woman suffers a reversal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setback for' reverses EVIL plus O as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive is a woman's given name.

clue.text: Dishevelled orchestra members, and how their instruments are played?

parts.note: the wind section of an orchestra plays woodwind and brass
wind instruments are blown to make a sound

explanation.surface: Untidy musicians in the band, and how they make music.
explanation.definitionFit: Windblown hair is messy and tousled, dishevelled by the breeze.

clue.text: Celebrity in traditional story

definitions.meaning: a famous person, a living icon
an old tale handed down, such as one about King Arthur

explanation.surface: A famous person appears in an old tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend means both a renowned figure and a traditional narrative.

clue.text: Young relative performing with king in light opera?

indicators.note: in places the king and the joining word inside the opera pair

parts.note: G and S is Gilbert and Sullivan, writers of comic operettas
R is Rex, Latin for king
and means together with
on means on stage, performing

explanation.surface: A youngster is performing alongside a king in a comic opera.
explanation.walkthrough: G and S is shorthand for Gilbert and Sullivan, the Victorian writers of comic operas such as The Mikado.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandson is a young relative, a child's son.

clue.text: Ducks and drakes, for example

parts.note: seems to name waterfowl hunted for sport, but also a pastime of skimming stones across water

explanation.definitionFit: Ducks and drakes is a pastime, and wild ducks are also birds shot for sport.

clue.text: Illegal activity, cleaning brass?

definitions.meaning: a crime, disguising the source of criminal profits
brass is British slang for cash, and cleaning it is making it look legitimate

explanation.definitionFit: Laundering dirty cash is a crime, figuratively washing money.

clue.text: Welsh river bird that's at stern of vessel?

parts.note: the Taff flows through Cardiff
a rail is a marsh bird

explanation.surface: A bird from a Welsh river perches at the back of a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A taffrail is the rail round the stern of a ship.

clue.text: Area of calm, as in French department, mostly

indicators.note: in puts the word as inside the shortened department
mostly says most of the word is used, its last letter gone

parts.note: Oise is a department of northern France
taken as written

explanation.surface: A peaceful spot found somewhere in a French region.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oise is a French department north of Paris; 'mostly' docks its last letter and 'in' does the enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is a figurative haven, a peaceful area amid turmoil.

clue.text: A neat end for one in the soup?

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox
a tail is the end of something

explanation.surface: A tidy finish for someone in deep trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' looks like an adjective, but it is the archaic word for cattle; 'in the soup' looks like 'in trouble'.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxtail is a meat used as the main ingredient of a classic soup.

clue.text: Easy, awfully, to stop when obsession departs, according to proverb

indicators.note: to stop means to plug a gap, so the scrambled letters fill the phrase

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
to have a thing about something is to be obsessed
goes means departs

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters are badly mangled

explanation.surface: Things become easy once an obsession fades, as the old saw has it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' scrambles EASY into ESAY; 'to stop' means to plug, and the obsession is a 'thing' you have about something.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase introduces a familiar saying, a proverb.

clue.text: Horse confused lady's led into church

indicators.note: into puts the mixed letters inside the church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: confused letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A muddled woman's horse is led into church.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a horse led into church; in fact 'confused' scrambles the lady's letters with 'led' (LYDESDAL), and 'into' sends them inside the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A Clydesdale is a heavy draught horse from Scotland.

clue.text: Works formerly right for introduction to Channel Islands?

indicators.note: for introduction to says the pieces are introduced, put inside

parts.note: once means formerly

explanation.surface: Works of the past are deemed right for bringing to Jersey and Guernsey.
explanation.definitionFit: Concerti are musical works, plural of concerto.

clue.text: Bird beginning to hide in cover under loose stones?

indicators.note: under says in this down clue the next piece sits below the stones

parts.note: scree is a slope of loose stones

indicators.note: in puts that first letter inside the cover

parts.note: a cowl is a hood or cover

indicators.note: beginning to takes the first letter of hide

explanation.surface: A bird starts to hide under a cover of stones.
explanation.definitionFit: The screech owl is a small owl species.

clue.text: Worker observed first of several cutters

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker
saw means observed

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of several

explanation.surface: A worker saw the first of several cutting tools.
explanation.definitionFit: Handsaws are saws worked by hand, cutting tools.

clue.text: Initially having little bread, fed by youth leader's sweetheart?

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of having
fed by means the other pieces are given something inside

parts.note: one bun is only a little bread

indicators.note: the youth leader is its first letter

explanation.surface: A youth leader feeds a hungry person with little bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one bun' is a cheeky reading of 'little bread'; 'fed by' sends the youth leader in between its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Honeybun is an affectionate term for a beloved, a darling.

clue.text: Note penned by popular navy medic

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed by the other pieces

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
RN is the Royal Navy
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A note is written by a popular navy doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned' looks like 'written', but it means shut in a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: An intern is a junior hospital doctor, especially in the US.

clue.text: Youngster from Salem, in Oregon

indicators.note: from says the letters are drawn out of the following words

explanation.surface: A youth from Salem in Oregon.
explanation.walkthrough: Salem is indeed the capital of Oregon.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor is a person below legal adulthood, a youngster.

clue.text: Unidentified writer's article about traditional drama

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the article goes around the drama

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
Noh or No is traditional Japanese masked drama

explanation.surface: An anonymous author's article about classical theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is short for anonymous, used where an author is unknown.
